tools.description: Pose the 3D avatar yourself: bones = {boneName: [x,y,z]} for ANY bone or node of the model (VRM humanoid names like hips, spine, head, leftUpperArm, rightLowerLeg, leftIndexProximal, or any other node from avatar_bones), expressions = {name: 0..1} (aa ih ou ee oh blink, plus any the model has), offsets = {node: [x,y,z]} metres, hips_offset = [x,y,z] metres, blend_ms (default 250). reset=true returns to rest. Humanoid bones use euler [x, y, z] radians in the VRM's normalized space; all zero is the T-pose (arms straight out); the avatar rests with arms down (leftUpperArm z=+1.25, rightUpperArm z=-1.25). Any other node of the model (ears, tail, hair roots, props) can be rotated by name too, as an offset from its own rest rotation, and moved with offsets={name:[x,y,z]} metres. Call avatar_bones to list every name. Other axes: experiment and look at the screen.
tools.name: avatar_pose

tools.description: Play your own animation on the 3D avatar: keyframes = [{t_ms, bones:{name:[x,y,z]}, expressions:{}, offsets:{}, hips_offset:[x,y,z]}] (up to 60 keyframes, 60 s), loop=true repeats. Values ease between keyframes; a bone not set in a keyframe keeps interpolating between the ones that set it, and starts from rest. Stop with avatar_pose reset=true. Humanoid bones use euler [x, y, z] radians in the VRM's normalized space; all zero is the T-pose (arms straight out); the avatar rests with arms down (leftUpperArm z=+1.25, rightUpperArm z=-1.25). Any other node of the model (ears, tail, hair roots, props) can be rotated by name too, as an offset from its own rest rotation, and moved with offsets={name:[x,y,z]} metres. Call avatar_bones to list every name. Other axes: experiment and look at the screen.
tools.name: avatar_animate
